name: Paliperidone
drug_class: Atypical (second-generation) antipsychotic; benzisoxazole (active metabolite of risperidone)
route_note: Oral extended-release (OROS) tablets once daily; IM palmitate depot monthly, every 3 months or every 6 months.

discovery.note: Developed as the principal active metabolite of risperidone, formulated for once-daily osmotic release and as long-acting palmitate ester.

tagline: Risperidone's active metabolite, best known as monthly to six-monthly injections
summary: Paliperidone is 9-hydroxyrisperidone, the major active metabolite of risperidone. It is used for schizophrenia and schizoaffective disorder, and its palmitate ester formulations allow injections as infrequently as twice a year, which can help adherence.
mechanism: Paliperidone antagonises dopamine D2 and serotonin 5-HT2A receptors, as well as alpha-1, alpha-2 and H1 receptors. Its pharmacology closely mirrors risperidone's.

Because it is largely excreted unchanged by the kidneys, it has fewer hepatic drug interactions but requires dose adjustment in renal impairment. The palmitate ester dissolves slowly from the muscle depot and is hydrolysed to paliperidone.

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: Oral Invega extended-release tablets are approved in December 2006.

history.title: Invega Sustenna
history.detail: Monthly paliperidone palmitate injection is approved; schizoaffective disorder indication follows.

history.title: DOJ settlement
history.detail: J&J's $2.2 billion settlement includes allegations of off-label promotion of Invega.

history.title: Invega Hafyera
history.detail: A six-monthly injection becomes the first twice-yearly antipsychotic.

pk.half_life: About 23 hours oral; weeks to months for palmitate depots

safety.boxed_warning: Increased mortality in elderly patients with dementia-related psychosis; not approved for this use.

facts: Invega Hafyera is given only twice a year after stabilisation on monthly or three-monthly injections.
